items.title: Do scale-dependent algorithms cut against a software intelligence explosion? (13 minute read)
items.snippet: Scale-dependent algorithms will cut against a software-only intelligence explosion. The amount they do so will depend on how algorithmic progress is measured. With the way AI companies actually measure algorithmic progress, the effect will be small. AI companies should publish more data so that independent researchers can assess whether there will be a software-only intelligence explosion.

items.title: Speculative Encoding: Many-to-Many Cache Translation (24 minute read)
items.snippet: Agents are increasingly passing context to one another as text. Speculative encoding translates hidden states directly from one model to another. It makes the model start answering faster than prefilling the text while keeping most of its accuracy. Prefill costs grow quadratically with context length, and prefill repeats much of what the sending model has already computed.

items.title: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths (6 hour read)
items.snippet: The exponent of square matrix multiplication is 9/4 over every field. A smaller exponent would compress tensor networks enough to violate a lower bound for testing whether the entries in each of several independent lists are distinct.
